title: What users are asking with Ask AI
description: [Ask AI](https://meta.discourse.org/t/search-better-in-your-community-with-ask-ai/411346) now has its own section on your admin dashboard at /admin. As admins, you can now see how people are using it and what they’re asking about.

title: Connect your AI apps to your community with Discourse’s built-in MCP server
description: Discourse now has a built-in MCP server, so you can ask your favourite AI apps to find a topic, catch up on a discussion, or prepare a report on activity in your community.

title: Introducing Discourse Workflows
description: Workflows includes a visual automation builder to create multi-step workflows with time delays, conditional branches, calls to external services, and AI actions directly in your admin area, letting you automate just about anything.

title: New filter and sort options for chat channels
description: We’ve just added the functionality to select filter and sorting options per section of chat channels! The defaults are unchanged, but now you can specify filter and sort options for each section (public channels, DM/group channels, and starred channels).

title: Edit dates, polls, tables, and more in the rich text editor
description: The rich text editor can now display and edit complex content types — dates, polls, tables, and graphviz diagrams — without requiring a switch back to the Markdown editor.

title: Users and topics shown on Signups, New Contributors, and Accepted Solutions reports
description: We’ve updated the Signups, New Contributors, and Accepted Solutions reports to show the specific users and posts behind the numbers.

title: Better Search with Ask AI
description: Ask AI helps your community get to the answers they want faster, by supporting natural language queries follow up questions. It also works ’side-by-side with the existing indexed search.

title: Drag-and-drop support for custom sidebar content
description: You can now drag links into the sidebar to add to existing custom sections or create new sections, and drag links within custom sections to reorder them in your sidebar.

title: Floating dismiss topics on mobile
description: Shows a floating 'Dismiss...' button on mobile for the topic list for easier access and to free up space in the top of the topic list. For new replies, the "Dismiss and stop tracking" option is in a submenu.

title: Suspend or silence users from the review queue
description: Staff can now suspend or silence users directly from the “User Needs Approval” and "queued-post" review items, without navigating to the admin page. Any active suspensions or silences are shown on the user card, making it clear why certain options are unavailable.

title: New sticky bar for pinned chat messages
description: Pinned chat messages now stay visible in a sticky bar at the top of the channel, where they can be easily accessed by channel members no matter when they join.

title: Redesigned admin dashboard
description: The redesigned admin dashboard lets you pin custom reports and includes improved site traffic, engagement, and other analytics tied to community success and value.

title: More accessible post images with Discourse AI
description: AI image captions can now be generated automatically for post images, making them more useful for screen readers, search, and image lightboxes.

title: Pinned emojis and bulk import/export custom emojis
description: You can now pin emoji groups to the top of the emoji picker, moving custom emojis groups to the top. New bulk import/export have also been added for custom emojis.

title: New category management area
description: We’ve created a complete directory of categories and their specific types for easier visibility and management.

title: Run Zoom webinars in your community
description: You can use livestream to host Zoom webinars directly in Discourse, so that members can watch the event and participate in the accompanying chat channel without leaving your community.

title: Improvements to RSS Polling plugin
description: The RSS Polling plugin has a fully rebuilt admin interface that makes it easier to configure feeds, validate them before they go live, and understand what’s happening with each poll.

title: Livestreams now built into Discourse Events
description: When creating a new event with a URL, you can now toggle livestream features in a single click. The stream link oneboxes alongside the event, and livestream chat is gated on event attendance.

title: Filter new users by activation status and bulk suspend options
description: The Admin > Users page now has a filter to easily surface unverified accounts on the New tab. You can now bulk suspend them alongside the existing bulk delete option, making it much easier to clean up spam registration waves.

title: Simpler email subject lines
description: Notification emails are now cleaner and simpler for your members. No more prefixes, brackets, tags, or category annotations. Enable the upcoming change to try it out.

title: High context topic cards are now enabled in the Horizon theme
description: Sites using the Horizon theme will now show richer topic cards with solved status, votes, assignee, tags, and excerpts, rolling out via an upcoming change. You can revert to simple cards anytime via a theme setting.

title: Discourse Reactions enabled by default for all sites
description: Reactions are now being rolled out to all new and existing sites via an upcoming change, ensuring no community has to miss out on this popular and engaging feature already used on many sites.

title: Livestream events now supported in the Events plugin
description: The Livestream plugin has been incorporated into the Events plugin, so you can run livestream events alongside standard virtual or in-person events through a single system.

title: Improvements to make it easier to create an event
description: We've made a number of improvements to make it easier to create events — including creating events directly from the calendar, editing the event directly in the composer, and more.
